newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Monday:
* Clinton Administration officials said they doubt they will reach an agreement this year to admit China to the World Trade Organization.
* Under the tax bill recently approved by Congress, Americans' right to roll over profits on old homes when they sell them and buy new ones is about to vanish.
* Seven regional wireless companies from the U.S. and Canada plan to unveil an alliance that would eventually allow customers to use the same mobile phone across the U.S.
* ITT Corp agreed to sell half its stake in the Desert Inn casino in Las Vegas and some adjoining land to financier Marvin Davis for $150 million in cash.
* United Parcel Service said its business was down as customers shifted to rival carriers amid a Teamsters strike against the company.
* Technology companies are overcoming their longstanding aversion to lobbying as a growing list of policy issues is debated in Washington that can affect their businesses.
* Britain's fifth non-cable non-satellite television service -- Channel 5 -- is still struggling to find its way, four months after its launch.
* Unhappy with the involvement of big companies like Warner Bros that had distributed his records in the past, the musician formerly known as Prince is attempting to self-promote his new album.
* More and more magazines are targeting overseas markets, altering their content to appeal to local tastes.
* Video-game players are increasingly spending their time and money at glorified arcade-playrooms that feature interactive technology.
* Barney's said Dickson Concepts would take control of the upscale, family-owned retailer.
* Niche long-distance companies that resell network time they buy from other companies are continuing to surge even as their suppliers -- the bigger carriers -- begin to stumble.
* Wired Ventures is reining in some of its empire-building efforts.
* Chris-Craft Industries is not eager to ink any acquisitions, despite its stockpile of roughly $1.5 billion in cash.
